findings: View bodies await network calls directly (bypassing any view-model layer): UpcomingRowView.swift lines 301/305/312 construct Radarr/Whisparr/SonarrClient inline inside a SwiftUI .task-driven closure to fetch file details; LibraryTabContent.swift lines 848/850 do the same for movie file lookups; SettingsView.swift line 229 constructs TMDBClient inline for a connection test button.

DetailView.swift is the heaviest per-call client constructor: 13 separate client-construction sites (lines 297-1401) each building a fresh Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr/WhisparrClient(config:) rather than reusing one instance, including inside monitor-toggle, search-trigger and file-fetch closures.

MediaEditPanel.swift, MediaDeletePanel.swift, and ReleaseListView.swift each re-implement an identical 4-arm switch (case .radarr/.sonarr/.lidarr/.whisparr: return XClient(config: configStore.x)) to pick a client by ServiceKind -- duplicated in at least 5 files (DetailView, MediaEditPanel, MediaDeletePanel, ReleaseListView, LocalToolBackend+CustomFormats).

Two synchronous read paths into view bodies confirmed: MediaServerIndex.posterURL(for:) (line 57) and MediaServerIndex.isWatched(for:) (line 64) -- both non-async, backed by the lock-guarded in-memory snapshot rather than an actor, explicitly to keep poster/watched-state resolution synchronous inside SwiftUI view bodies per CLAUDE.md's documented pattern.

ChatToolCatalog.swift declares 29 tools; each maps to a handler split across 8 LocalToolBackend+*.swift files (ArrTools 1000 lines covering ~8 tools, Discover 494 lines / 3 tools, TMDB 300 lines / 3 tools, Library 320 lines, MediaServer 107 lines / 3 tools, TitleDetails 125 lines / 1 tool, CustomFormats 186 lines / 1 tool) -- LocalToolBackend+ArrTools.swift alone is 1000 lines covering roughly half the catalog and is the largest single migration unit.

ArrMCPServer reaches the same 29 tools only through two thin bridge files (ToolCatalogBridge.swift 26 lines, MCPCallRouter.swift 97 lines) that wrap a LocalToolBackend instance -- the MCP server has zero direct client-construction sites of its own; all tool execution funnels through ArrCore's LocalToolBackend, so migrating LocalToolBackend's dependencies to MediaKit automatically carries the MCP server along with it.

TMDB-related call sites (tmdb_search_person, tmdb_discover_movie/tv, PersonStore's credit fetches) show no DemoMode.isActive branch at their exact construction line -- unlike every arr/download-client/media-server call, which is gated -- but the same files (TrailerProvider 3x, CastProvider 3x, CountryProvider 2x, PersonStore 3x) do show DemoMode.isActive hits elsewhere per file, so this needs closer reading before concluding TMDB demo coverage is actually missing; flagged in open_questions.

DemoMode.isActive occurs at much higher density in transport files (SearchClient.swift 10x, ArrAPIClient.swift 11x, SonarrClient/LidarrClient 8x each, RadarrClient 6x) versus Views/ViewModels (ServerStatusModel 1x, QueueViewModel 8x, SearchViewModel 2x, ChatViewModelHolder 2x) -- confirms the branch logic is concentrated in the transport layer (the MediaKit-bound half) rather than presentation.

ConfigStore keys arr configs per-ServiceKind via ArrBarr.config.<rawValue> in UserDefaults (ConfigStore.key(_:), line 891) -- one ServiceConfig instance per ServiceKind case, confirmed by the @Published properties at lines 51-60 (radarr/sonarr/lidarr/whisparr/sabnzbd/qbittorrent/nzbget/transmission/rtorrent/deluge) plus a single non-keyed mediaServer: MediaServerConfig (line 167), consistent with CLAUDE.md's 'ONE of Plex/Jellyfin/Emby' rule.

QueueViewModel observes ConfigStore via 5 separate Combine .debounce(for: .seconds(1.5), scheduler: DispatchQueue.main) pipelines (lines 290, 311, 318, 324, 330) -- all using the same 1.5s constant, not a shared named constant, so a future change to the debounce window requires editing 5 sites.
loc lint (Tools/loc/lint_missing_keys.py) ran clean today: '0 code-referenced keys missing from catalog'.

All 14 #available/@available(macOS 26 / iOS 26, ...) gates outside Packages/TonightCore are concentrated in exactly 6 files: PopoverContentView.swift (3), QuizSettingsPane.swift (1), iOSAppRoot.swift (1), GlassyFloatingBar.swift (4), ChatViewModelFactory.swift (1), FoundationModelsProvider.swift (4) -- all Views/Services in ArrCore, none in the app or widget targets.

The widget target (ArrBarrWidgets.swift, 666 lines) never constructs a raw Radarr/Sonarr/etc client directly -- it goes through LibrarySummaryService() and UpcomingService() (both per-call constructed, not shared singletons) reading ServiceConfig via ConfigStore-backed values passed in, and falls back to DemoMocks.upcoming directly on line 490/511 when unconfigured -- a widget-specific inline demo-data path distinct from the DemoMode.isActive branches used elsewhere.

AppIntents (ArrBarrIntents.swift, 242 lines, 6 intents) do not construct arr clients themselves: they build a shared LocalToolBackend via makeBackend() (line 14) for read intents, and call QueueViewModel.shared.pause/resume (lines 173, 194) for the two write intents -- only 3 of the 6 intents (ShowDownloadQueue, ShowUpcoming, CheckArrHealth) are exposed to Siri/Shortcuts via ArrBarrAppShortcuts in ArrBarr/ArrBarrApp.swift; SearchToAddIntent, PauseAllDownloadsIntent, ResumeAllDownloadsIntent exist but have no AppShortcut phrase wired.

13 supporting transport/aggregation files total 13071 lines of code that are candidates for replaced_by_mediakit=true (RadarrClient 609, SonarrClient 733, LidarrClient 513, WhisparrClient 324, SearchClient 594, 6 download clients 1412 combined, HTTPClient 352, 5 MediaServer files 1057 combined, QueueAggregator 695, DownloadDropService 157, DownloadProgressService 140, LibraryIndex 215, LibrarySummaryService 36, UpcomingService 43, SpotlightIndexer 508, SeriesIdentityResolver 201, TMDBClient 620, CastProvider 105, PersonStore 136, CountryProvider 63, TrailerProvider 77, ConnectionHealthMonitor 115, 9 DemoMocks* files 2749 combined, DemoMonitorState 90, DemoQueueState 50, ConfigStore 1077 kept in ArrCore) -- see files list for the full per-file breakdown with exact wc -l counts.
open_questions: The combined single-command client-construction grep returned 123 total lines while the sum of per-directory grep counts (Views 57 + ViewModels 10 + Services 116 + AppIntents 0 + ArrMCPServer 0 + app/widget/shared 0 = 183) is inconsistent -- likely because the first combined grep call passed multiple directory args to one invocation with different matching behavior than looping per-directory; recommend the coordinator re-run a single canonical command per directory rather than trusting the 123 aggregate figure.

Whether TMDB traffic is deliberately excluded from DemoMode's network short-circuit (no DemoMode.isActive branch found at the exact TMDBClient/PersonStore/CastProvider/CountryProvider/TrailerProvider construction lines grepped, despite those very files having nonzero DemoMode.isActive hit counts elsewhere) needs a closer read of those 5 files' actual demo-branch placement before treating it as a confirmed gap.

Endpoint path templates for the 6 download clients (qBittorrent/Transmission/Deluge/rTorrent/SABnzbd/NZBGet) and the 3 media-server clients (Plex/Jellyfin/Emby) were inferred from public API knowledge, not from reading each client file's actual request-building code line by line -- treat the operations table's 'path' values for those rows as best-effort approximations pending a direct read of QbittorrentClient.swift, TransmissionClient.swift, DelugeClient.swift, RtorrentClient.swift, SabnzbdClient.swift, NzbgetClient.swift, PlexClient.swift, JellyfinClient.swift; no separate Emby client file was found under Services/MediaServer -- unconfirmed whether Emby is handled by branching inside MediaServerClientFactory/one of the two existing files or is unimplemented.

summary: Read-only inventory of ArrBarr's communication-layer consumers ahead of the MediaKit migration. Mapped every construction site of the 13 client types (Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr/Whisparr/TMDB/SearchClient/6 download clients/MediaServerClientFactory) across Views (57 hits), ViewModels (10), and Services (116), with DetailView.swift as the single worst offender (13 per-call constructions) and at least 5 files duplicating an identical ServiceKind-switch client picker. Catalogued the 29-tool ChatToolCatalog and its 8 LocalToolBackend+*.swift implementation files (3041 total lines), confirmed ArrMCPServer reaches all 29 tools purely by wrapping LocalToolBackend through two thin bridge files (123 lines total) with zero client construction of its own. Enumerated 6 AppIntents (3 exposed via AppShortcutsProvider) and the widget's fetch path (LibrarySummaryService/UpcomingService, never raw clients, with an inline DemoMocks.upcoming fallback). Listed 13 NotificationCenter.post sites against 10 declared Notification.Name constants (mostly navigation, not data-layer), 22 static-shared singletons, and Swift-concurrency density (55 actor decls, 124 @MainActor, 73 nonisolated occurrences). Documented ConfigStore's 46 @Published properties (1077 lines) and confirmed one ServiceConfig instance per ServiceKind keyed as ArrBarr.config.<rawValue> plus a single non-keyed mediaServer config; QueueViewModel observes it through 5 identical 1.5s Combine debounce pipelines. Ran the loc lint script clean (0 missing keys) and grepped all 14 macOS/iOS 26 availability gates outside TonightCore, all confined to 6 ArrCore files. Built a 44-row network-operations table distinguishing reads from 9 write-mutating endpoints (search-trigger, monitor-toggle, add-to-library, delete, pause/resume, media-server scan) and which are demo-gated. Marked replaced_by_mediakit=true with exact line counts for all 13071 lines across 40 transport/client/cache/demo-mock files, and false for views, view-models, ConfigStore, QueueViewModel, AppIntents, notification wiring and the widget target.
